sampling_model.design: Independent stratified sampling from \(E\) fixed environments with deterministic counts \(n_e\).
sampling_model.units: Within each environment, \((T_{e,i},Y_{e,i})_{i=1}^{n_e}\) are independent draws from \(P_e\), and samples are independent across environments.
sampling_model.treatment: The treatment is generated by \(T_e=\alpha U_e+\epsilon_{t,e}\); there is no randomized assignment.
sampling_model.overlap: Not applicable; identification comes from environmental cumulant shifts rather than treatment propensity overlap.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Cumulants through \(R_{\max}\) are estimated by symmetrized \(U\)-statistics, \(A\) by the rank-\(d\) SVD of \(\widehat C\), and the projected-moment influence covariance by leave-one-out first projections.  Independent Gaussian multipliers and vanishing Gaussian jitters provide the covariance-adaptive Anderson--Rubin calibration; reported coverage integrates over all auxiliary draws.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 3.6 proves that \(\beta\) is not identifiable from two environments when both \(\epsilon_u\) and \(\epsilon_t\) change.
Theorem 1 gives uniqueness of the BACKSHIFT joint diagonalizer if and only if every pair of intervention-variance profiles is nonproportional across environments.
Theorem 3.1 makes Causal Dantzig invariance identical to GMM moments, and regular GMM theory yields asymptotic normality and optimal weighting.
The paper's SR-AR and SR-CQLR tests have uniformly correct asymptotic size without restrictions on identification strength or moment-covariance eigenvalues.
Causal Dantzig identifies a linear causal coefficient through an invertible covariance-difference moment and gives regular low-dimensional confidence intervals.
Under perfect interventions, one intervention on each latent node is sufficient and worst-case necessary for coupled-cumulant recovery of linear causal disentanglement parameters.
Higher-order cumulants identify latent-variable LiNGAM effects when a proxy or underspecified instruments provide auxiliary source information.
The paper characterizes bivariate effect identifiability by exogenous-noise Gaussianity without auxiliary variables.

body.tldr: Simultaneous changes in latent and treatment noises create an exact source-label ambiguity.  When environment-indexed latent cumulant shifts occupy an unknown calibrated \(d\)-plane, the orthogonal flag \(Q_Ac_k\) identifies \(\beta\) at its first nonzero order, while global absence of a flag admits a legal unequal-effect source swap.  The environment threshold \(E=d+2\), every first identifying order, and the weak-breakout estimation and honest-length rates are sharp on the stated domains.  The same-sample estimated-plane influence expansion now also yields an implementable Gaussian-multiplier Anderson--Rubin inversion: vanishing Gaussian jitter gives asymptotically exact unconditional coverage uniformly through singular, rank-changing, and zero influence covariance.

project_justification.gap: The closest higher-moment paper handles two environments and either one changing component or simultaneous-shift nonidentification.  It explicitly leaves open whether environments can identify an effect jointly when pairwise comparisons fail.  Covariance-based multi-environment methods use a different diagonal-shift geometry and cannot resolve the treatment-versus-latent source label in this model.
project_justification.niche: A low-rank restriction on latent environmental cumulant profiles creates a joint geometric signal that is invisible to every pairwise analysis.  The resulting first-breakout order is simultaneously an identification boundary, an environment-design resource, and a statistical strength parameter.
project_justification.fill: The project gives an if-and-only-if observed-law frontier, an explicit compatible-bounds construction proving that its no-breakout branch contains interior unequal-effect laws, a sharp \(d+2\) environment threshold, realizable lower-order-indistinguishable models at every cumulant order, universal rate upper bounds, matching lower bounds on one compatible experiment, a uniform generated-projector expansion, and a covariance-adaptive Gaussian-multiplier Anderson--Rubin inversion whose vanishing jitter handles atomic critical laws.

body.related_work: Kivva, Akbari, Salehkaleybar, and Kiyavash (2025), especially Theorem 3.6 and its source-swap proof, supply the closest obstruction and the mixed-cumulant algebra; their local analytic-mgf antecedent is weaker than the globally finite-mgf restriction maintained here.  The present target answers their stated multi-environment question under a new low-rank profile restriction and is positioned as informed by, rather than as a strict tightening of, that theorem.  Rothenhäusler, Heinze, Peters, and Meinshausen (2015) give BACKSHIFT's contrasting covariance joint-diagonalization condition; that paper does not support the present loading, calibration-rank, or calibration-gap restrictions.  Cai et al. (2023), Leyes Carreno, Meroni, and Seigal (2025), and Tramontano et al. (2025) demonstrate higher-cumulant recovery under one-latent-component, targeted-intervention, proxy, or instrumental structure; none supplies the environmental source-label frontier here.  Li, Kwok, Guo, and Liu (2026) characterize effect identifiability from one bivariate law according to noise Gaussianity and publicly exclude constrained multi-environment settings from scope; the complete proof text was externally inaccessible during this scan, so the paper is treated only as an informed-by comparator.  Long et al. (2023) provide the environmental GMM template in a regular supplied-moment model.  Andrews and Guggenberger (2019) provide singularity-robust Anderson--Rubin inference for high-level supplied moments and do not support the primitive source moment envelope or the same-sample cumulant-plane correction.  Davis and Kahan (1970) are cited solely for stability of an estimated spectral projector under matrix perturbation.  Causal Dantzig supplies regular covariance-shift inference.  None of these results supplies the present leave-one-out covariance replacement bound or the vanishing-jitter calibration through zero and rank-changing influence covariance.  Mooij, Magliacane, and Claassen (2020) explain why unknown intervention targets, latent confounding, and feedback are material in the Sachs application, while Sachs et al. (2005) provide the multi-perturbation single-cell setting rather than evidence that the new latent-profile condition holds.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The covariance-adaptive Anderson--Rubin result is asymptotic, fixed-dimensional, and uses the maintained \(2R_{\max}+\delta\) moment envelope, the fixed calibration gap, leave-one-out influence estimates, a diverging number of Monte Carlo draws, and external Gaussian jitter.  It permits singular, rank-changing, and zero influence covariance but does not promise finite-sample exactness, conditional-on-randomization coverage, or exact deterministic threshold calibration at an atom.  The full-observation minimax lower-bound family remains established on one fixed compatible bounded experiment, not on every arbitrary nonempty bounded shell.
body.honest_scope: The identification if-and-only-if is confined to the explicitly source-labelled union \(\mathcal D_\rho\), not arbitrary simultaneous shifts.  The explicit no-breakout construction proves nonemptiness only for fixed bounds admitting positive model constants that satisfy the displayed interior, singular-gap, and moment inequalities; incompatible bounds carry no nonemptiness claim.  The entire-mgf condition is newly maintained here as a strict global strengthening of the local analytic-mgf antecedent used by Kivva et al.  The \(d=1,E=2\) reduction is already known from Kivva et al., Theorem 3.6, and the no-breakout honest-length proposition is an incremental standard consequence.  A failed finite scan through \(R_{\max}\) does not establish global no-breakout outside this domain.  The Sachs data motivate the consumer but do not verify the structural restrictions.  The original deterministic-radius Anderson--Rubin interval remains the finite-sample conservative guarantee.  The Gaussian-multiplier refinement has asymptotically exact unconditional coverage over the declared first-breakout shells because its auxiliary jitter vanishes; without such randomization, strict and weak deterministic single-threshold rules need not attain an intermediate nominal probability at an atom.
